applicability.jurisdiction_or_standard_context: Statics and direct-stiffness/FEM concept guidance from open educational sources; not a complete element load-vector derivation.

claims.text: A distributed load can often be replaced by an equivalent resultant for statics equilibrium reasoning, with magnitude and location tied to the distribution.

source_refs.locator: Applications of the direct stiffness method

claims.text: Solver-ready loads in stiffness workflows may be nodal loads, member/element loads, equivalent nodal actions, or fixed-end actions depending on the element formulation and load type.
Fraia run artifacts should preserve both authored load intent and resolved solver load representation so reactions and downstream design actions can be audited.

limitations: Equivalent static resultants are not always enough to preserve member force and displacement behaviour in analysis.
Exact load vector derivations belong to solver/element implementation docs.

pages_used: Applications of the direct stiffness method

summary: Fraia should keep authored load assignments distinct from the solver-ready loads and equivalent actions produced during realization.
title: Load Application and Equivalent Loads
